mainTopic: The end of the blind-witness sugya, then רבי אבא's rulings sent to רב יוסף בר חמא (a father naming one son, a wife's share like a son, and a disputed loan) and the ruling that the הלכה follows them.
overview: The amud opens by closing the earlier sugya: one source refutes all the אמוראים who let a witness who later went blind testify. Then רבי אבא sends a series of rulings to רב יוסף בר חמא. The first ruling is unclear: a father who says something about 'a child among the sons' is נאמן, while רבי יוחנן says he is not. אביי reads it as leaving all one's property to one son. רבא objects that 'believed' does not fit that case, and he reads it instead as a father naming his בכור. The second ruling says a wife told to 'take like one of the sons' gets a son's share. רבא adds that this covers only current property, and her share counts sons born later. The third ruling deals with a loan where the מלוה, the לוה and the עדים each tell a different story. The לוה swears, and the מלוה collects half, but only from free property. The גמרא shows this works even for רבי עקיבא, and מר בר רב אשי argues the reverse. מר זוטרא rules that the הלכה follows all of רבי אבא's rulings. רב אשי explains that this does not clash with רב נחמן. The amud ends by asking whom the ruling excludes, and the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Final refutation of all the earlier views
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא closes the earlier sugya. The opinions of all the אמוראים who allowed a witness who went blind to testify are refuted.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a refutation of all of them! It is indeed a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is closing the previous discussion by declaring that all the opposing opinions have been refuted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, a source was brought that went against several אמוראים. The גמרא now says that one source knocks out all of them at once, and it confirms that the refutation stands. The earlier topic is now finished.

keyTerms.meaning: A conclusive refutation; an opinion is shown to be wrong by a source
Of all of them

steps.whatToRemember: The earlier sugya ends with a full refutation of everyone who allowed a witness who went blind to testify.

phrases.english: A refutation of all of them!
phrases.notes: 'All of them' means all the אמוראים who allowed a witness who later went blind to testify.

phrases.english: It is indeed a refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the sugya from before this point.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: All the opinions that let a witness who went blind testify are refuted.

steps.title: רבי אבא's message: a father speaking about one child
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא sends a ruling to רב יוסף בר חמא: a man who says something about one child among his sons is נאמן, but רבי יוחנן says he is not נאמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא sent to רב יוסף בר חמא: One who speaks about a child among the sons is believed. And רבי יוחנן says he is not believed.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רבי אבא reports a ruling and a disagreeing view from רבי יוחנן, but he does not say what the father actually said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling is short and leaves out the key detail. We do not know whether the father said 'this one is my firstborn,' 'this one inherits everything,' or something else. This gap sets up the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: Sent (a message or ruling)
One who says
A child among the sons
Believed; his word is accepted
Not believed

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume you already know what the father said. The ruling leaves it out on purpose, and the rest of the sugya tries to figure it out.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלַח רַבִּי אַבָּא לְרַב יוֹסֵף בַּר חָמָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba sent to Rav Yosef bar Chama:

phrases.aramaic: הָאוֹמֵר עַל תִּינוֹק בֵּין הַבָּנִים – נֶאֱמָן.
phrases.english: One who says something about a child among the sons is believed.
phrases.notes: The text never says what he said about the child. That is the puzzle the גמרא takes up next.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan says: he is not believed.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַח רַבִּי אַבָּא לְרַב יוֹסֵף בַּר חָמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new sugya after the previous one closed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A father's statement about one child among his sons is accepted according to one view, and not accepted according to רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: What does רבי אבא mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי אבא's unclear ruling means.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for an explanation of רבי אבא's ruling. This sets up אביי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling does not say what the father declared about the child, so it cannot be understood yet. The גמרא needs to know which case is under discussion before it can analyze the dispute.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he saying? (a request to explain an unclear statement)

phrases.english: What is he saying?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the ruling in step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exactly the father said about the child, and what the dispute is about.

steps.title: אביי: it is about leaving everything to one son
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the father said 'this child will inherit all my property.' The first view follows רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, and רבי יוחנן follows the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: This is what he means. One who says about a child among the sons, 'He shall inherit all my property,' is believed, like רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה. And רבי יוחנן says he is not believed, like the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question. He says the case is a father declaring that one son will inherit everything, and he links the two views to a known מחלוקת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה holds that a father may choose one of his heirs to inherit all his property, so the statement takes effect. The רבנן disagree, so according to them the statement does nothing. אביי reads 'נאמן' and 'אינו נאמן' as 'his statement works' and 'his statement does not work.'

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he means (introduces an explanation)
He shall inherit all my property
The Sages, who disagree with him

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן (the אמורא) is a different person from רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה (the תנא). In אביי's reading they take opposite sides.

phrases.english: Abaye said: This is what he means,
One who says about a child among the sons:
"He shall inherit all my property" is believed,
in line with Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אֵינוֹ נֶאֱמָן, כְּרַבָּנַן.
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan says: he is not believed, in line with the Rabbis.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The case is a father saying 'he shall inherit all my property.' The dispute matches רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה against the רבנן.

steps.title: רבא: the wording does not fit אביי's reading
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects: if the issue is inheritance, the ruling should have said 'he inherits' or 'he does not inherit,' not 'believed' or 'not believed.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא objected: Is this 'believed' and 'not believed'?! It should have said 'he inherits' and 'he does not inherit'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges אביי's explanation from the wording of רבי אבא's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'believed' and 'not believed' are about trusting someone's claim of a fact. Choosing an heir is not about trust; it is about whether the father has the power to do it. So 'נאמן' points to a statement of fact, which suggests אביי has the wrong case in mind.

keyTerms.meaning: Objects to it; attacks the previous explanation
He should have said

steps.whyThisMatters: This pushes the גמרא to look for a case where the father is really testifying about a fact, so that 'believed' fits.

phrases.english: Rava objected to it:
Is this a matter of "believed" and "not believed"?!
He should have said "he inherits" and "he does not inherit"!

steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's reading that the case is about leaving all one's property to one son.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Believed' is about trusting a claim of fact, but giving an inheritance is about legal power. The ruling's wording therefore does not fit אביי's case.

steps.title: רבא explains the ruling as being about a firstborn
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a new reading of רבי אבא's ruling. A father who says 'he is my בכור' is believed according to רבי יהודה, and רבי יוחנן says he is not believed, following the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said this is what רבי אבא meant: if a man says about one child among his sons, 'he is the firstborn,' he is believed, like רבי יהודה. And רבי יוחנן says he is not believed, like the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: Step 5 knocked down אביי's explanation, so רבא now offers his own reading of רבי אבא's unclear ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's objection was that the words 'believed / not believed' do not fit a gift of inheritance. So he moves the case to a question of believability: does a father's word decide which son is the בכור? This fits the wording and ties into the מחלוקת between רבי יהודה and the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Firstborn son, who receives a double portion of the inheritance
A child
'This is what he is saying,' used to introduce an explanation of someone's words
The Sages, here the ones who disagree with רבי יהודה

steps.whatToRemember: The final reading of רבי אבא's first ruling: the question is whether a father is believed to say which son is the בכור. רבי יהודה says yes; the רבנן, followed by רבי יוחנן, say no.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
This is what he (Rabbi Abba) is saying:
One who says about a child among his sons:
'He is the firstborn' is believed,
in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda.
phrases.notes: This points back to רבי יהודה's view that a father is believed to say which son is the firstborn, discussed a little earlier on 127b.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan says: he is not believed,
in accordance with the Rabbis.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces אביי's explanation, which was rejected in step 5, with a reading that fits the words 'believed / not believed.'
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What case was רבי אבא's unclear ruling about?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A father who says one son is the בכור. He is believed according to רבי יהודה and not believed according to the רבנן, whom רבי יוחנן follows.

steps.title: A wife who takes a share like one of the sons
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא sends a second ruling: if a man says 'my wife should take like one of the sons,' she takes a son's share.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא sent to רב יוסף בר חמא: if a man says, 'My wife should take a share like one of the sons,' she takes a share like one of the sons.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling that רבי אבא sent, about a man who gives his wife a share of his property equal to a son's share.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wife does not normally inherit from her husband. Here, though, the husband's words work like a gift, so they take effect and she receives a portion the size of one son's share.

keyTerms.meaning: He sent to him, meaning a ruling sent in a letter or by a messenger
She shall take
My wife

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלַח לֵיהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא לְרַב יוֹסֵף בַּר חָמָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba sent to Rav Yosef bar Chama:
One who says: 'My wife shall take like one of the sons,'
she takes like one of the sons.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַח לֵיהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא לְרַב יוֹסֵף בַּר חָמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ruling in the same series of rulings that רבי אבא sent to רב יוסף בר חמא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A husband who says his wife should take like one of the sons gives her a share equal to one son's portion.

steps.title: רבא limits and defines the wife's share
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains two limits. The gift covers only the property the husband owns now. Her share is counted by including sons born later.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: this applies to the property he owns now, and it counts the sons who will be born afterward.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds two details that explain how רבי אבא's ruling about the wife works in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because her share works as a gift, it can only take effect on property the husband already owns, not property he gets later. When figuring her share, we count every son, including those born after he spoke, so her portion matches what each son ends up with.

keyTerms.meaning: Property he owns right now
After this point, later on

steps.confusionAlert: The two parts of רבא's statement deal with different things. 'Current property' sets which property is given. 'Sons born later' sets how big her slice is. They are not saying the same thing.

phrases.english: Rava said:
And only with regard to his current property,
and including sons who come afterward.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets the limits of רבי אבא's ruling about the wife's share.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The wife's share comes only from the husband's current property, and it is figured by counting future sons as well.

steps.title: Three different claims about a loan document
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא's third ruling covers three accounts of a loan. The מלוה says nothing was paid, the לוה says half was paid, and the עדים say all was paid. The לוה swears, and the מלוה collects half, but only from בני חורין, not from משועבדין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא sent to רב יוסף בר חמא: someone brings a loan document against another person. The lender says, 'I was not paid anything.' The borrower says, 'I paid half.' The witnesses say he paid all of it. The borrower swears, and the lender collects half from free property. But he cannot collect from sold property, because the buyers say, 'We rely on the witnesses.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third ruling from רבי אבא about a loan where the lender, the borrower and the witnesses each give a different account.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The לוה admits to part of the claim, so he swears that he paid half. He then owes the other half because of his own admission. The עדים say everything was paid, so the buyers who bought his land can rely on them. That is why the מלוה cannot take that land from the buyers.

keyTerms.meaning: A loan document
The lender
The borrower
Free property the borrower still owns
Property the borrower sold after taking the loan, which was tied to the debt

steps.confusionAlert: Notice who swears and who collects. The לוה swears about the half he says he paid. The מלוה collects the other half.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלַח לֵיהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא לְרַב יוֹסֵף בַּר חָמָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba sent to Rav Yosef bar Chama:
One who brings out a loan document against his fellow;
the lender says: I was not paid anything,
and the borrower says: I paid half,
and the witnesses testify that he paid all of it,
this one (the borrower) swears,
and he (the lender) collects half from free property;
but not from sold property,
because they (the buyers) say: We rely on the witnesses.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַח לֵיהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא לְרַב יוֹסֵף בַּר חָמָא: הַמּוֹצִיא שְׁטַר חוֹב עַל חֲבֵירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The third ruling in the series that רבי אבא sent to רב יוסף בר חמא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the לוה admits half but the עדים say he paid everything, the לוה swears. The מלוה collects half from בני חורין but not from משועבדין, since the buyers rely on the עדים.

steps.title: Why the oath applies even according to רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that even רבי עקיבא, who treats a partial admitter as a משיב אבידה and frees him from the oath, would agree here. When there are עדים, the לוה is afraid to deny everything.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even according to רבי עקיבא, who says he is like someone returning a lost object, that applies only where there are no witnesses. But where there are witnesses, he is afraid to deny everything.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers an unspoken question: doesn't רבי עקיבא free this kind of borrower from swearing? It shows that רבי אבא's ruling works even according to רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא frees a partial admitter from the oath when his admission is like returning a lost object, meaning he could have denied it and gotten away with it. When there are עדים, he could not safely deny everything, so his admission is not a free gift. He is simply afraid, and so the normal oath for admitting part of a claim applies.

keyTerms.meaning: One who returns a lost object, who is freed from swearing because he volunteered the truth
'These words apply,' used to limit a rule to a certain case
He was truly afraid

steps.whatToRemember: An admission only counts as 'returning a lost object' when the person could have denied everything without risk. When there are עדים, fear pushes him to admit, so the oath stays.

phrases.english: And even according to Rabbi Akiva,
who says: he is like one who returns a lost object,
these words apply where there are no witnesses,
but where there are witnesses,
he is afraid.
phrases.notes: Literally 'he was truly afraid.' With witnesses around, he wouldn't dare deny the whole loan, so his admission isn't a favor.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲפִילּוּ לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, דְּאָמַר: מֵשִׁיב אֲבֵדָה הָוֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends the oath in step 9 against a possible objection based on רבי עקיבא's view.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: no עדים versus עדים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: According to רבי עקיבא, the לוה who admits half should be exempt from the oath as a משיב אבידה.
steps.terutzMaskana: When there are עדים, the לוה admits out of fear and not as a free gift, so even רבי עקיבא would require the oath.

steps.title: מר בר רב אשי argues the opposite: with witnesses, the borrower is like one who returns a lost item
steps.stepSummary: מר בר רב אשי pushes back on the previous step. He says that when עדים support the לוה, even רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, who usually treats a partial admitter as a מודה מקצת הטענה, would agree he is a משיב אבידה.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בר רב אשי objects: It is the other way around! Even רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, who says such a person counts as one who admits part of the claim, only says so when no witnesses back him up. But when witnesses do back him up, he is surely like someone returning a lost item.
steps.whatsHappening: מר בר רב אשי flips the argument from step 10. He says the witnesses help the לוה. They do not make him nervous.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 said the עדים make the לוה afraid to deny everything, so his partial admission is a normal admission and he must swear. מר בר רב אשי says the reverse. The עדים say he paid everything, yet he honestly admits half is still owed, so he is like someone returning a lost item. This challenges רבי אבא's ruling that the לוה must swear.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary; it is the other way around
One who admits part of the claim, and normally must swear about the rest
One who returns a lost item; someone who volunteers money he did not have to give, so he is exempt from an oath
They support him; they help his side

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two opinions. רבי עקיבא usually calls a partial admitter a משיב אבידה. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר usually calls him a מודה מקצת הטענה. מר בר רב אשי says that in this case, with עדים, even רבי שמעון בן אלעזר would agree he is a משיב אבידה.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Mar bar Rav Ashi objects to this:
On the contrary,
even according to Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar
who says: he counts as one who admits part of the claim,
that applies only where there are no witnesses
who support him,
but where there are witnesses
who support him,
phrases.notes: The witnesses say he paid everything, which is even better for him than his own claim of half.

phrases.english: he is certainly one who returns a lost item.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי: אַדְּרַבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reverses the reasoning of step 10 about how the עדים affect the לוה.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 10's claim that the עדים make the לוה afraid, and through it רבי אבא's ruling that the לוה swears.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The עדים support the לוה's side. If he admits half anyway, he is volunteering money, so he is a משיב אבידה and should be exempt from the oath, even according to רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.

steps.title: מר זוטרא rules that the law follows all of רבי אבא's rulings
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא, quoting רב שימי בר אשי, rules that the הלכה follows every one of the rulings that רבי אבא sent to רב יוסף בר חמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא taught in the name of רב שימי בר אשי: The הלכה in all these rulings is as רבי אבא sent to רב יוסף בר חמא.
steps.whatsHappening: After all the discussion, מר זוטרא gives the practical ruling. We follow everything רבי אבא sent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ruling covers the whole group of rulings from רבי אבא's letter, including the loan case just discussed. So in practice the לוה does swear, as רבי אבא said. The next steps test whether this ruling clashes with רב נחמן.

keyTerms.meaning: Taught publicly
The practical law
Rulings or teachings

steps.whyThisMatters: It turns רבי אבא's letter of rulings into practical הלכה.

phrases.english: Mar Zutra taught
in the name of Rav Shimi bar Ashi:
The law in all these rulings
is as Rabbi Abba sent
to Rav Yosef bar Ḥama.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the debate to the practical ruling on all of רבי אבא's teachings.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows all of רבי אבא's rulings.

steps.title: רבינא asks about רב נחמן's disagreement
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks רב אשי how this ruling fits with רב נחמן, who disagreed with one of רבי אבא's rulings.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: What about the ruling where רב נחמן disagreed?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא points to a possible problem. רב נחמן disagreed with one of רבי אבא's rulings, so does מר זוטרא's ruling cover that one too?
steps.deeperAnalysis: One of רבי אבא's rulings was about collecting a debt from slaves the borrower left to his heirs, and רב נחמן disagreed about it. Usually we follow רב נחמן in money cases. So רבינא wants to know whose view wins on that point.

keyTerms.meaning: What? What is the law?

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:
What about that of Rav Naḥman?
phrases.notes: He means the ruling about collecting from slaves left to the heirs, where רב נחמן disagreed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי: דְּרַב נַחְמָן, מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how far מר זוטרא's ruling reaches.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the ruling 'follow all of רבי אבא' include the ruling where רב נחמן disagreed?

steps.title: רב אשי: we learn it as 'one does not collect,' just like רב נחמן
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that in their version, רבי אבא's ruling says 'אין גובין', meaning one does not collect from the slaves. That is exactly what רב נחמן said, so there is no clash.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: We learn it as 'one does not collect,' and רב נחמן said the same.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי removes the problem. His version of רבי אבא's ruling agrees with רב נחמן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא assumed רבי אבא said a creditor collects from slaves left to the heirs. רב אשי learns it the other way, 'אין גובין'. So רבי אבא and רב נחמן agree, and there is nothing to decide between them.

keyTerms.meaning: One does not collect the debt
We learn it this way; this is our version

phrases.english: He said to him:
We learn it as 'one does not collect,'
phrases.notes: Our version of רבי אבא's ruling says the creditor can't collect from the slaves left to the heirs.

phrases.english: and so said Rav Naḥman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא's question by giving a different version of רבי אבא's ruling.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אבא's ruling reads 'אין גובין', which agrees with רב נחמן, so there is no conflict.

steps.title: If everyone agrees, what is the ruling meant to exclude?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if רב נחמן agrees with רבי אבא, then whom is מר זוטרא ruling against when he says 'the הלכה is'?
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, the statement 'the הלכה is like רבי אבא' comes to exclude what?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new question that sets up the next discussion. It asks what opposing view מר זוטרא's ruling rejects.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ruling of 'הלכתא' usually decides between people who disagree. Once רב אשי showed that רב נחמן agrees, there seems to be nobody left to rule against. The answer will come in the next part of the גמרא.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude what? Which other view is this rejecting?

phrases.english: But then, 'the law is'
comes to exclude what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רב אשי's answer, which seems to leave מר זוטרא's ruling with no one to disagree with.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which opposing opinion does מר זוטרא's ruling of 'הלכתא' reject?
